LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorIndi: The decoding error indicator for a true value x and observation y is true when the estimate d(y) differs from x, and false otherwise.
The error indicator is true exactly when d(y) ≠ x.
The error indicator is false exactly when d(y) = x.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProb: For the joint law p of a source X and observation Y, the error probability is the probability of the event d(Y) ≠ X.
For X and Y defined on a common discrete source, the decoding error probability is obtained from their joint distribution and equals Pr[d(Y) ≠ X].
Under source law p, the error probability of d(Y) as an estimate of X equals the real probability of the set of outcomes ω with d(Y(ω)) ≠ X(ω).
For a finite joint law, the error probability is the sum of p(x,y) over all pairs with d(y) ≠ x.
For any joint law of a source and observation, a decoder's error probability is nonnegative.
For any joint law of a source and observation, a decoder's error probability is at most one.
Under any discrete source law, the probability that d(Y) differs from X is nonnegative.
Under any discrete source law, the probability that d(Y) differs from X is at most one.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_decodingE: For any joint law of (X,Y), the entropy of the decoding error indicator equals h(e), the binary entropy of e = Pr[d(Y) ≠ X].
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_decodin: Under the source law p, the Boolean variable indicating d(Y) ≠ X has entropy h(e), where e is its probability of being true.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_fano: For a joint law on finite alphabets, let m be the source alphabet size and e = Pr[d(Y) ≠ X]. If m ≥ 2, H(X|Y) ≤ h(e) + e ln(m−1), where h is binary entropy in nats. For m = 1, the conditional entropy, the error and the bound are all zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_fano_: For a joint law on finite alphabets and decoding error e, H(X|Y) is at most the m-ary entropy hₘ(e), where m is the source alphabet size and hₘ(e) = h(e) + e ln(m−1) for m ≥ 2.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_fan: For finite-valued X and Y on a common discrete source, let m be the size of the alphabet of X and e = Pr[d(Y) ≠ X]. If m ≥ 2, H(X|Y) ≤ h(e) + e ln(m−1), where h is binary entropy in nats. For m = 1 the conditional entropy, the error and the bound are all zero.
For finite-valued X and Y, H(X|Y) is at most hₘ(e), the m-ary entropy of the decoding error e, where m is the size of the alphabet of X. For m ≥ 2, hₘ(e) = h(e) + e ln(m−1).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_fano_: For a finite joint law with m possible source symbols and error probability e, H(X|Y) ≤ ln 2 + e ln m.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_fan: For finite-valued X and Y, if X has alphabet size m and d(Y) has error probability e, then H(X|Y) ≤ ln 2 + e ln m.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProb: For a joint law on finite alphabets, every decoder of X from Y has error probability at least (H(X|Y) − ln 2)/ln m when the source alphabet has m ≥ 2 symbols.
For finite-valued X and Y with source alphabet size m ≥ 2, the probability that d(Y) differs from X is at least (H(X|Y) − ln 2)/ln m.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_fano_l: For a finite joint law whose source marginal is uniform on m ≥ 1 symbols, I(X;Y) ≥ (1−e) ln m − ln 2, where e is the decoding error probability.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_fano: If X is uniform on m ≥ 1 symbols and Y is finite-valued, I(X;Y) ≥ (1−e) ln m − ln 2 for any decoder with error probability e.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProb: For a finite joint law with source marginal uniform on m ≥ 2 symbols, the error probability of any decoder is at least 1 − (I(X;Y) + ln 2)/ln m.
If X is uniform on m ≥ 2 symbols and Y is finite-valued, the probability that d(Y) differs from X is at least 1 − (I(X;Y) + ln 2)/ln m.
